Holohory Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Jews lived in Holohory from 1470, building a synagogue in the early 17th century; the population reached 1,216 (44 percent) by 1880, served by rabbis including Mordekhai-Arieh Heber (1910–1915), Shlomo Schickler (from 1927), and Yosef-Mordekhai Bloom. In January 1942, a ghetto held 575 Jews before their November 1942 deportation to the Zolochiv ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection, where they shared the fate of the local community. This cemetery, in use until WWII, was demolished in the 1960s-70s, per local residents, with its tombstones used to build a sugar factory in Krasne and a kolkhoz in Holohory.
